title: renders are refused by the launch args of the live :8188 instance while the 4090 has room (19.6GiB free vs ask 18GiB)
evidence: port 8188 answering, free=19.6GiB vs ask 18GiB (so free VRAM is NOT the cause), claim=idle; the :8188 instance (pid 553489, owner foreign, holder operator) was launched WITHOUT --reserve-vram, so `ensure` refuses on the ARGS before it ever asks the scheduler for a claim — this refusal is about the launch line, not about how much VRAM is free (see COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM). Response: the OPERATOR's interactive session -- a human is using the shared install; yield the window, do not touch/restart/re-flag it (a running process's args are not ours to change); the harness yields the window rather than submitting to an unflagged instance, so renders stay blocked until that instance exits or is relaunched with --reserve-vram. Nothing here is ours to restart.

notes.note: 2026-09-23 13:4xZ ops-triage: DECISION = keep open, route stays AGENT (self-closing; NOT a second ask). This check is the DIFFERENTIAL: it fires only when the launch-args gate refuses while the live free reading ALREADY clears the ask the harness would make (13:3xZ: 22.2GiB free vs ask 21GiB, pid 553489 reserve=missing, claim=idle) — the case no VRAM arithmetic can explain and the shape that let an earlier starvation read as 'nothing is blocking us'. It stays on the agent queue deliberately: render-starved (route=tim) already carries the same fact in its evidence AND now in a live-sized ask, so a second tim item would be the duplicate escalation this board exists to remove. No remedy here is ours (an unflagged instance cannot be rendered through — that is the measured over-commit OOM — and a foreign session is not ours to restart or re-flag). Self-closes the moment that instance exits or is relaunched with --reserve-vram.
